Subject: Billing details for pilot (fractional tokens & long history bundling)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of technical questions we need clarified before we can sign the pilot SOW: specifically how Redwood handles fractional-token rounding when a request is under the minimum quantum, and how you amortize long-history / conversation bundles across the invoice line items.

Two concrete scenarios we need samples for (we'll put these into our SOW appendix):
1) A streaming request that generates 37.4 tokens billed against a 50-token minimum quantum — is that rounded up to 50, or do you aggregate across the session and prorate?
2) A clinical-chat with 120k of user+assistant context ingested over a month, but only ~18k tokens actively used per day — how do you break that into invoiceable buckets if someone replays history vs. prefix reuse?

Can you send simple invoice-line examples and a short note on what pilot credits you can apply if our usage bumps up during onboarding? Attached the SOW draft for context.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Billing details for pilot (fractional tokens & long history bundling)

Hi Maria — thanks, and great questions. Quick answers up front, followed by two short invoice examples and a suggested pilot concession.

1) Minimum quantum and fractional tokens: Redwood charges at the configured quantum for the route. For a 50-token quantum, a single call that uses 37.4 tokens will be billed as 50 tokens unless you enable session aggregation (recommended for chat-heavy workloads). Session aggregation groups calls within the same session/window so partial tokens can net out across exchanges; when enabled we sum true token usage across the window and then apply the quantum rounding to the window total.

2) Long-history / bundling: We treat two dimensions separately — active per-call token usage (per-token generation/consumption) and stored context footprint. For replayed history that is re-sent on request, those tokens are billed as normal per-call tokens. For prefix reuse or cached KV (where we materialize a reusable embedding/prefix) we offer a "context bundle" SKU that amortizes the ingest cost across a chosen retention window (monthly by default). That SKU appears as a separate invoice line (Context Bundle - 30d) and gets prorated daily if the bundle is created mid-cycle.

Attached are two short examples (also placed in the spreadsheet you sent):
- Example A (single-call quantum billing): one 37.4-token call on a 50-token route -> billed as 50 tokens; invoice line: 1 x 50 tokens @ $0.0008 = $0.04.
- Example B (session aggregation): same session has five calls totaling 210.8 tokens, quantum 50 -> window sum 210.8 -> rounded up to 250 tokens -> billed as 250 tokens; invoice line: 1 x 250 tokens @ $0.0008 = $0.20.

Pilot concession we can offer: a one-time onboarding credit equal to the first two invoice cycles' context-bundle charges up to $8,000, provided the pilot converts to a committed Dedicated capacity within 90 days. If you don't convert, standard billing applies and we can discuss a smaller non-commit credit.

I'll let Ben add the formal invoice-line wording and Tessa can confirm the pilot credit language for the SOW. If you want, we can convert these examples into sample invoice rows for the SOW appendix and run them past procurement.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: GF_Billing_Examples.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi all — jumping in with formal invoice wording and the rounding rule we use in contracts. Rachel covered the behavioral details; I'll add the exact phrasing for the SOW so procurement can place it in the terms.

Contract clause (billing):
- "Token Consumption: Tokens are meterable units representing subword pieces used or generated by the Service. Billing is calculated per Billing Route at the configured quantum. For a given Billing Window, Token Usage is summed and rounded up to the nearest configured quantum. Single-call usage is billed at the configured quantum if session aggregation is not enabled.
- Context Bundles: Context Bundles are billed as a separate SKU representing deduplicated stored context; charges are prorated daily if the bundle is created or deleted mid-cycle. Replayed history sent within a call is billed as per-call tokens and not charged against stored bundle amortization unless materialized as a bundle by mutual agreement."

Sample invoice rows (plain text to paste into SOW appendix):
1) ROUTE-CHAT-XS | Quantity: 1 | Units: 50 tokens | Unit price: $0.0008 | Line total: $0.04 (single-call < quantum)
2) ROUTE-CHAT-XS | Quantity: 1 | Units: 250 tokens | Unit price: $0.0008 | Line total: $0.20 (session-agg rounded)
3) CONTEXT-BUNDLE-30D | Quantity: 1 | Units: 1 bundle-month | Unit price: $400 | Line total: $400 (prorated if mid-cycle)

A couple of nuance calls out: if you expect many small single exchanges, enable session aggregation with a 24h window for the pilot — that'll typically reduce the ineffective overhead from quantum rounding. If instead your traffic is highly spiky with many independent single calls, we can set a custom quantum for that route.

Rachel — happy to draft a short SOW appendix with the exact lines. Maria — would you like us to put these on Greenfield's SOW as-is or do you prefer we provide a redlined paragraph for your legal team?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
